transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-10
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Mendez (CTO, Kestrel), Ravi Kapoor (ML Lead), Grace Lin (Platform Eng)

Auto-generated Summary (may be noisy):
Kestrel Telecom is evaluating Redwood for a mixed deployment: hosted for prototypes, dedicated for latency-sensitive inference, and private/VPC for regulated customer data. Primary concerns: 8k+ context length for multi-turn customer call summarization, multilingual (EN/ES/FR) support, function/tool-calling for lookups (billing, account retrieval), and SSO/KMS for customer data. Redwood team to run benchmarks (2k vs 8k tokens) on customer samples and share Dedicated/Private pricing/security docs.

Topics: model selection (open models), context length and chunking, tool-calling/function calls, multilingual inference, deployment mode tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), security (SOC2/KMS/SSO), benchmarks and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam: hey everyone thanks for joining, sorry we ran a bit late on our side, i'm liam from redwood, i'm the AE, with priya the se. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sofia: doing well, thanks — Sofia here. shoutout, we got about 45 minutes, hope that's okay.
[00:10] Priya: great, thank you. quick agenda: run through Kestrel's goals, constraints, sample workload, then dig into model/context options and tool-calling. we'll keep notes and call out action items.
[00:21] Ravi: good. short background — we process customer support calls across 6 regions, mostly English and Spanish, plus some French. current infra is microservices on k8s, we stream calls to an internal ASR then do NLU. looking for a model path to do: verbatim summarization, entity extraction, reranking answers against internal KBs, and function calls to hit billing/account endpoints. timeline: pilot in Q1, production late Q1/early Q2.
[00:45] Grace: additionally latency matters for the live agent assist scenario — we need tail latency under 250ms for partial replies in the agent UI, but batch offline jobs can tolerate higher.
[01:02] Liam: ok — so two distinct workloads: low-latency streaming for agent assist, and long-context batch summarization for call transcripts. do you have any constraints on data residency or encryption?
[01:12] Sofia: yes, some customer data must stay in-region for EU customers, and enterprise customers want KMS + HSM support ideally. SOC2 compliance is required.
[01:23] Priya: that's all supported — Redwood Private offers customer-managed KMS and on-prem options; Dedicated has KMS integrations and an SLA. we'll include the SOC2 attestation in the pack.
[01:34] Ravi: great. on models, we were looking at Llama-2-70b, Mistral, and Mosaic variants, maybe also MPT for the summarization. curious about quantized variants for cost. beginner question: how do you pick for multilingual + tool-calling?
[01:50] Priya: good question. short answer: pick a model that has strong multilingual coverage and supports function calling patterns you need; smaller quantized variants can be fine for retrieval+rerank. for long-context (8k+), we recommend models with native long context or using chunking + KV cache. Redwood's runtime does prefix caching and continuous batching which helps the per-token cost.
[02:10] Ravi: when you say KV cache — is that in memory on the GPU? we had someone refer to 'KV cash' in a demo and got confused.
[02:18] Priya: yeah ha, 'KV cash' is the meme — it's KV cache, it's GPU resident memory for key/value attention states. reduces recompute for multi-turns. for 8k context if the model supports it natively, latency is lower; otherwise we do chunking and stitch outputs, which can add overhead.
[02:36] Sofia: are there open models you'd recommend for bilingual (EN/ES) summarization specifically?
[02:42] Priya: empirically we've seen Mistral-8x and Llama-2-13b (with Llama-2-70b for higher quality) perform well across EN/ES. MPT family can be tuned for summarization. If you need 8k context and lower cost, sometimes a quantized 13b or 33b with 8k window works best. We'll test both native long-window models and chunked approaches.
[03:05] Grace: what about function calling — do models need special training or is it a runtime pattern?
[03:12] Priya: function-calling is mostly a prompting + structured-output pattern, some models are better at following schemas. Redwood supports structured output enforcement and tool-calling orchestration so you can register endpoints (billing.lookup, account.get, etc.) and the runtime will route. For safety we support verification steps and a fallback policy.
[03:31] Ravi: latency for function call round-trips — if the model decides to call an internal API, that adds external network latency. how do you manage that?
[03:39] Priya: common patterns: 1) do local retrieval first (embedding search on a cached index) to avoid network calls, 2) parallelize long-running calls, 3) have timeouts and partial responses. Redwood's trace view can show you token vs external-call latency. for tight agent assist we often pre-fetch likely entities.
[03:58] Liam: curious about cost tradeoffs — are there rough per-1k-token numbers for hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[04:05] Priya: we'll send a pricing matrix but rough: hosted is easiest but can be premium per-token; dedicated reduces unit cost with reserved capacity; private has infra and license fees but gives isolation. quantized models (4-bit, 8-bit) materially reduce GPU RAM and cost. exact numbers will depend on throughput and batch sizes.
[04:28] Sofia: on the security side, any concerns with function-calling triggering data egress?
[04:33] Priya: in hosted we have controls and data policies; Dedicated can be VPC-restricted and Private keeps control plane in your network. we'll detail KMS and HSM integration, audit logs, and SSO in the security pack.
[04:47] Ravi: about multilingual evaluation — we can provide a bilingual dataset, but how do you recommend we evaluate?
[04:53] Priya: provide a representative sample: 200 short calls and 50 long calls, include transcripts + reference summaries in EN/ES. We'll run evals for ROUGE/BERTScore and a small human pass for quality checks. Also test structured entity extraction accuracy and function-call correctness.
[05:11] Grace: for streaming partials in agent UI, do you recommend shard-by-sentence or stream-as-generated? we're worried about flicker and partial hallucinations.
[05:20] Priya: stream-as-generated works if you use prefix caching and gating rules — Redwood can emit partial tokens while the model keeps generating. We recommend UI-level debounce and semantic chunking (emit stable sentences). Also using a reranker for suggested responses reduces hallucinations.
[05:39] Sofia: any gotchas with quantized models and function-calling reliability? we've heard quantized sometimes changes phrasing.
[05:47] Priya: true — some aggressive quantization can slightly degrade token-level fidelity and schema-following. that's why we test quantized variants on your schema-heavy prompts. fallback is to run critical calls on a higher-precision variant. Redwood's rollout policies can route schema-sensitive calls to a non-quantized variant automatically.
[06:05] Ravi: are you able to do custom fine-tuning or only prompt engineering?
[06:10] Priya: for Hosted we curate open models and allow instruction tuning via prompt templates; Dedicated and Private customers can bring tuned checkpoints or we can help with fine-tuning workflows. note that fine-tuning has data governance implications — we'll include that in the security docs.
[06:25] Liam: let's talk benchmarks — Priya, can you outline what you'll run?
[06:29] Priya: sure. plan: 1) throughput/latency for 2k and 8k sequences across 3 model variants (Llama-2-13b, Mistral-8x, quantized 13b), 2) structured-output fidelity test for function calls using 50 schema cases, 3) multilingual summarization quality on customer samples (EN/ES). I'll provide a spreadsheet with results.
[06:52] Ravi: sounds good. do you need GPU access or any special infra from us?
[06:56] Priya: we'll run in our Redwood staging infra for apples-to-apples numbers, but we can also run a bring-your-own-image test on your infra if you prefer Private later. For now staging is faster.
[07:07] Grace: from platform side, what integration hooks do you offer? we run k8s with Istio and have internal auth for APIs.
[07:14] Priya: Redwood provides REST + SDK clients, webhooks for callbacks, and a connector model for VPC private links. SSO/SAML can integrate with your IdP and we can register RBAC roles. We'll include config snippets for Istio sidecars in the security pack.
[07:30] Sofia: any reference customers in telecom or similar real-time use cases?
[07:34] Liam: we have a couple — will share anonymized case studies (one on retail contact centers with streaming agent assist, one on a regulated enterprise using Private deployment).
[07:44] Ravi: on fallback policies — you mentioned automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity is constrained, how deterministic is that?
[07:51] Priya: you configure policy thresholds (latency, error rate, cost). Redwood will fall back to a compatible variant and we emit a header indicating fallback so you can track in logs and metrics.
